I just use "inmaakazijn", a vinegar made for pickling and add herbs. You can also just buy vinegar (5%min), mix it with water 1:1, that is really all there is too it. You can also use 1/4th lemonjuice and 3/4th water. You want an absolute minimum of 0,8% of acid in the fluid to kill bacteria.

As for the herbs, it depends. If you want to pickle something like courgette, use onions, celeryseed, mustardseed, mustardpowder, yellowrootpowder, and some sugar. Standard recipes call for 300-500 grams, so use 100 or less, assuming 1 liter of fluid, I only use sugar for courgette and aubergine. For pickles use salt, peppercorns, korianderseed, mustardseed, dash of ginger and piment, dill, clove, kardemom, maybe some bay tree leaves. Simply boil the mixture with herbs in it, clean the weck jar with boiling water and soda, dry it, fill with whatever you wish to pickle, 40% fluid 60% stuff to be pickled. Herbs are to taste, so experiment a bit. Before I had to pickle my own pickles, the only thing I made this way was atjar, using seeds and cloves, little anise for extra freshness.
